verses.text: I, Paul, beg you by the gentleness and kindness of Christ. Some say that I am shy when I am with you, but bold towards you when I am away.
I beg you, do not make me be bold when I come. I expect I will have to be bold with some people who think we live in a worldly way.
We do live in the world, but we do not fight our battles the way the world does.
The weapons we fight with are not the world's weapons. They have God's power to pull down strong places.
We pull down every argument and every proud idea that stands against knowing God. We take every thought captive and make it obey Christ.
And once you have fully obeyed, we will be ready to punish every act of not obeying.
You are looking only at what is in front of your eyes. If anyone is sure that he belongs to Christ, he should think again. We belong to Christ just as much as he does.
Even if I boast a little too much about the authority the Lord gave us, I am not ashamed. He gave it to us to build you up, not to tear you down.
I do not want it to seem that I am trying to frighten you with my letters.
Some people say, "His letters are strong and powerful, but in person he is weak, and his speaking is nothing special."
Such people should know this: what we say in our letters when we are away, we will do when we are there.

We do not dare to put ourselves in the same group as some who praise themselves, or to compare ourselves with them. They measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves. That shows they do not understand.
But we will not boast beyond the limits. We will keep within the area of work God gave us, and that area reaches all the way to you.
We are not going too far by boasting about you, as if we had not reached you. We were the first to come all the way to you with the good news of Christ.
We do not boast about work done by others, beyond our limits. We hope that as your faith grows, our area of work among you will grow much bigger.
Then we can preach the good news in places beyond you. We do not want to boast about work already done in someone else's area.
But, "Whoever boasts should boast about the Lord."
It is not the one who praises himself who is approved. It is the one whom the Lord praises.
